To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the introduction of a new computer system into a public child welfare agency did not have an adverse impact on workers' job attitudes.

(1) workers' satisfaction with a computer system is low; (2) workers' attitudes toward their agency do not change as a result of the introduction of a new computer system; (3) workers' expectations about the system are exaggerated beyond the reality of what actually occurs; (4) workers' expectations for the system are not affected by their attitudes toward the agency; and (5) workers' expectations of computer systems are not affected by the level of computer knowledge they possess.

the introduction of computer technology to a large public welfare agency did not have a significant impact on workers' satisfaction with their jobs and their agency, but did have a significant impact in changing workers' attitudes about the computers themselves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of computerization on job attitudes in the public child welfare agency.
the impact of computer technology on child welfare workers.
the impact of the use of computers on the attitudes and job satisfaction of workers in the public sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the introduction of computerized case information systems to large public welfare departments does not appear to have a significant impact on the attitudes of workers toward the department or their jobs.
the introduction of the new system did not significantly affect the workers' attitudes toward their jobs or their agencies.
the introduction of the computerized system did not have a negative effect on the attitudes of the workers toward the agency or their jobs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the computerization of the case record in child protective services has been a failure.
the introduction of a new technology into a social agency is not a simple process.
the computer system had little effect upon workers' job satisfaction and job attitudes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
workers' attitudes toward computers and their work are not necessarily related to the actual impact that computers have on their work.
the introduction of a new information technology is a major organizational change, and the impact of such change on workers is likely to be substantial.

computerization is a process that is not complete with implementation, but is a process that continues to change the nature of the job, and that the attitudes and expectations of workers need to be considered as the process continues.
